title: Voice (sustained sung vowels)
reference_instrument: adult male voice, sustained vowels (VocalSet long tones, CC BY 4.0)
summary: Sustained vowels on C3, C4 and F4, with no words. The tract is another man's, from MRI of spoken German vowels; he isn't the singer on any page. Every page is cleaner than its recording, by 2.7 to 24.0 dB, and we haven't shown why. The spectrum's tilt follows his vowels, not the singers'. A two-mass vocal fold model self-oscillates against that tract, and the sound is read at a simulated microphone 0.30 m from the mouth, 45 degrees off axis. No source waveform or formant filter is applied. One scale on the fold stiffnesses, trimmed on the model alone, puts each card near its written note, so pitch isn't evidence. The graded notes are straight tones with slow pitch movement and no vibrato. The phrases carry vibrato, and each vowel there is its own render, joined by crossfades. The /a/ at six pitches and the vowel ladder further down are older renders on earlier tracts.
physics_present: Two-mass vocal folds on Ishizaka and Flanagan's 1972 law as printed, for the glottal flow and the forces on the masses, as a mirror pair, with masses and base stiffnesses from the licensed model-card pack. The oscillation isn't imposed: it comes from the fold, the flow, collision and the tract loop.

A measured tract on every page: subject 1 of the Dresden Vocal Tract Dataset (Birkholz et al. 2020, CC0), a man in MRI of spoken German vowels, tense or lax by a rule fixed before any grade. The cut from his 3-D model to one dimension is ours (91 to 113 sections), and the dataset's own printed area functions aren't used.
Viscothermal loss and a flanged-piston mouth load from the transfer-matrix duct.
The cited yielding wall (the Flanagan setting as given by Birkholz, Haesner and Kuerbis 2022) on all 14 cards, including C4-u-rigid, whose name comes from an older comparison.
Sound at the microphone: mouth flow radiated through a baffled circular opening, 0.30 m away at 45 degrees off axis. The pressure inside the tract is never the output.
Slow pitch movement on the straight-tone notes (Ternström and Friberg 1989 model; amplitude from choir singers told to sing straight), moving the three fold stiffnesses and set for each card.
Vibrato on the phrases only, in place of the slow pitch movement: 5.9 Hz and +-69.5 cents, the means of 50 professional singers (Larrouy-Maestri, Magis and Morsomme 2014).

A glottal jet noise row (Verge 1995 flue-jet constant, extrapolated to the glottis). Its gate is a flow threshold, so it sounds for part of each note at C4 and F4, only briefly at C3, and not at all on the C3 /i/ page.
Breath pressure that rises over 150 ms, the centre of a speech range (Fant and Kruckenberg 2005), and is then held.
Folds retrimmed per card on the model alone: only the three fold stiffnesses move, no recording enters, and the tract's passive formants don't change.
physics_missing: The singer's own tract: these are one man's spoken vowels, and larynx height, pharynx and lip shape differ in singing. The spectrum's tilt follows his vowels, not the singers', and 1-2 kHz is further from the recordings than on the earlier cards on most pages.

An explanation for how clean it is: every page is cleaner than its recording, by 2.7 to 24.0 dB, more than on the pages before this tract on most notes, and we haven't shown why. The jet noise row is the only noise source on these cards.
Words, consonants and moving tract shapes: tract shape and fold settings are fixed within a render, and each join between vowels in the phrases is a crossfade.
Vibrato and slow pitch movement together: the engine takes one gesture on the fold's tension. There are no register changes or formant-tuning gestures.

The singers' tuning and pitch movement: the cards are trimmed to the written note and sit -15.5 to +8.5 cents from equal temperament, while the recordings sit -48.4 to +10.0 cents from it. The period swing over the middle of a clip is 19.3 to 43.6 cents (5-95 %), against 11.5 to 100.6 cents in the recordings.
A sung onset: the pressure rise is a speech value from one male speaker, and no adduction gesture is entered. Attacks read 27 to 65 ms against 22 to 580 ms in the recordings.

Fold tissue: a lumped two-mass card, not layered body-cover tissue or a 3-D fold. The damping and collision values are printed typical values of one model, not measurements of a voice, and one stiffness scale per card stands in for a fold-elongation law.
Lungs and trachea: the subglottal pressure is an authored player input on each card, not a measured one, with no lung or trachea coupling.
Tract acoustics beyond a single series chain of plane-wave sections: no cross-modes, nasal coupling or side branches.
His tense /u/: the engine's frequency check refuses that tract, so lax /u/ stands in.

The wall's detail: it's uniform along the tract, not a measured distribution, and its stiffness is an assumption because the source neglects it. His first formants on these cards sit 49 to 63 Hz above the print's measured ones. That gap is the wall and 37 C air against a rigid model at room temperature, and we haven't split the two.
Head and torso: an infinite baffle replaces them, so there's no head diffraction. The receiver's resolved band is 8 kHz, so energy above that isn't a prediction.
A measured breath: the tract air is a declared physiological state, not a cited measurement.
Convergence on these cards: no ladder has been run on the tract cards, and the fold clock's earlier ladder used a different tract and law.
